sources.ref_file_title: BGW05 - Collusion Resistant Broadcast Encryption with Short Ciphertexts and Private Keys
sources.authors: Dan Boneh, Craig Gentry, Brent Waters
sources.note: Reference page already exists in the wiki.

pages.class_justification: The construction uses the pairing group only through group operations and the pairing map. The static-security proof is one fixed reduction that receives a decisional n-BDHE instance, programs the public key and the corrupted users' private keys around the adversary's committed target set, and invokes the BE adversary once as an oracle to answer the BDHE challenge - the RTV04 fully-black-box shape (fixed construction, reduction black-box in the adversary).
pages.model_justification: No random oracles; plain public parameters, standard-model proof.
pages.statement: A bilinear group in which the decisional $n$-BDHE (bilinear Diffie-Hellman exponent) assumption - a $q$-type strengthening of [[bilinear-map-assumptions|BDH]] - holds yields a fully collusion-resistant [[broadcast-encryption|BE]] scheme for $n$ users with $O(1)$-size ciphertexts and private keys and an $O(n)$-size public key; security is static: the adversary commits to the target set before setup - [[BGW05 - Collusion Resistant Broadcast Encryption with Short Ciphertexts and Private Keys|BGW05]].
pages.sketch: Public parameters are the powers $g^{\alpha^i}$ for $i \in \{1,\ldots,2n\} \setminus \{n+1\}$ together with $v = g^\gamma$, and user $i$ holds $d_i = g^{\gamma\alpha^i}$; the session key $e(g,g)^{\alpha^{n+1}t}$ can be assembled by any member of the target set from $d_i$ and the published powers, while $g^{\alpha^{n+1}}$ itself is never published. The static reduction embeds a decisional $n$-BDHE challenge into exactly these powers and runs the adversary once.
flags: Hypothesis granularity: BGW05 needs decisional n-BDHE, a q-type assumption not defined on the bilinear-map-assumptions page; consider a separate BDHE node and re-pointing this edge
The O(1)-ciphertext efficiency claim comes with an O(n)-size public key, now stated explicitly

pages.wrong_reason: The claim's basis is 'BDDH -> short signatures (BLS) - standard', a misattribution: BLS unforgeability is proved under the computational co-CDH assumption in the random-oracle model (Boneh-Lynn-Shacham, 'Short Signatures from the Weil Pairing', ASIACRYPT 2001), not under decisional BDH; no BLS proof from BDDH exists. The wiki already records the correct edge as red-co-cdh-to-ds (model rom). Digital signatures do follow from BDH hardness via the composite chain BDH => DLOG hard => OWF => DS, but composite chains must be split per the schema and that chain is not what this page or its source text asserts.

sources.ref_file_title: LW10 - New Techniques for Dual System Encryption and Fully Secure HIBE with Short Ciphertexts
sources.note: Verified via eprint 2009/482 and the TCC 2010 proceedings (DOI 10.1007/978-3-642-11799-2_27).

pages.class_justification: The construction uses the pairing group only through its group and pairing operations. The dual system proof is a fixed hybrid sequence over the adversary's key queries; each hybrid step is a reduction that runs the HIBE adversary once as an oracle against a DLIN or DBDH challenge, with no dependence on the adversary's code.
pages.model_justification: The point of Wat09 is a standard-model proof: no random oracles, no q-type assumptions.
pages.statement: If the decisional bilinear Diffie-Hellman and decisional Linear assumptions ([[bilinear-map-assumptions|DBDH and DLIN]]) hold in a symmetric pairing group, there is an adaptively (fully) secure [[hierarchical-identity-based-encryption|HIBE]] in the standard model, with security loss polynomial in the number of key queries rather than exponential in the hierarchy depth - [[Wat09 - Dual System Encryption Realizing Fully Secure IBE and HIBE under Simple Assumptions|Wat09]].
pages.sketch: The proof switches the challenge ciphertext and then each of the adversary's key queries to semi-functional form one hybrid at a time; each switch is a black-box reduction to DLIN, and a final DBDH step hides the message, so an adaptive adversary with $q$ key queries yields a distinguisher for one of the two assumptions with $O(q)$ loss.
pages.improvements_text: - Fully secure HIBE with short ciphertexts, via dual system encryption in composite-order groups - [[LW10 - New Techniques for Dual System Encryption and Fully Secure HIBE with Short Ciphertexts|LW10]]

pages.class_justification: The construction uses the pairing group only through its group and pairing operations. The dual system proof is a fixed hybrid sequence: each step runs the IBE adversary once as an oracle against a DLIN or DBDH challenge and never inspects the adversary's code.
pages.model_justification: Standard-model proof; no random oracles (this, plus the simple assumptions, is the paper's contribution).
pages.statement: If the decisional bilinear Diffie-Hellman and decisional Linear assumptions ([[bilinear-map-assumptions|DBDH and DLIN]]) hold in a symmetric pairing group, there is an adaptively secure [[identity-based-encryption|IBE]] whose ciphertexts, private keys, and public parameters each consist of a constant number of group elements; the proof is in the standard model via dual system encryption - [[Wat09 - Dual System Encryption Realizing Fully Secure IBE and HIBE under Simple Assumptions|Wat09]].

pages.wrong_reason: The slug pins this edge to Gro16, but Gro16 does not prove a NIZK from BDH/DLIN or any falsifiable bilinear assumption: Groth16's knowledge-soundness proof is in the generic (bilinear) group model, an edge the wiki already records as red-bilinear-pairing-to-snark-gro16 (class free, model generic-group), and basing it on a falsifiable assumption via black-box reduction is ruled out by the existing barrier no-falsifiable-assumption-to-snark-gro16 (Gentry-Wichs). sources.ref_file_title: KZG10 - Constant-size commitments to polynomials and their applications
sources.authors: Aniket Kate, Gregory M. Zaverucha, Ian Goldberg
sources.note: Reference page already exists in the wiki.

pages.class_justification: One fixed construction that uses the bilinear group only through group operations and the pairing, and one fixed security reduction: an adversary breaking evaluation binding outputs two accepting openings of the same commitment at the same point, from which the reduction algebraically computes $g^{1/(\tau - z)}$, a $t$-SDH solution, using the adversary once as an oracle.
pages.model_justification: Requires a structured reference string $(g, g^\tau, \ldots, g^{\tau^t})$ for a secret $\tau$ (trusted setup); the SRS is a structured CRS.
pages.statement: Given a [[pairings|bilinear pairing]] and a structured reference string $(g, g^\tau, \ldots, g^{\tau^t})$ with $\tau$ secret, a prover can commit to any $f \in \FF_p[X]$ of degree at most $t$ with a single group element and prove any evaluation $f(z) = y$ with a single group element; evaluation binding holds under the [[q-strong-diffie-hellman|$t$-SDH]] assumption, and the Pedersen variant is additionally unconditionally hiding - [[KZG10 - Constant-size commitments to polynomials and their applications|KZG10]].
pages.sketch: Commit as $C = g^{f(\tau)}$, computed from the SRS; to open at $z$, publish $w = g^{\psi(\tau)}$ for the quotient $\psi(X) = (f(X) - f(z))/(X - z)$, and verify $e(C/g^{y}, g) = e(w, g^{\tau}/g^{z})$. Two accepting openings of $C$ at $z$ with values $y \ne y'$ give $(w/w')^{1/(y'-y)} = g^{1/(\tau - z)}$, breaking $t$-SDH.
